review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

3:1.sourceText: Πέτρος δὲ καὶ Ἰωάνης ἀνέβαινον εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπὶ τὴν ὥραν τῆς προσευχῆς τὴν ἐνάτην.
3:1.targetText: One afternoon Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.

groups.note: BSB renders the δέ that opens this new episode as One afternoon, a setting drawn from the ninth hour.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
ὥραν ("hour") is stated once; BSB repeats it in the apposition the ninth hour.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:2.sourceText: καί τις ἀνὴρ χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχων ἐβαστάζετο, ὃν ἐτίθουν καθ’ ἡμέραν πρὸς τὴν θύραν τοῦ ἱεροῦ τὴν λεγομένην Ὡραίαν τοῦ αἰτεῖν ἐλεημοσύνην παρὰ τῶν εἰσπορευομένων εἰς τὸ ἱερόν·
3:2.targetText: And a man who was lame from birth was being carried to the temple gate called Beautiful, where he was put every day to beg from those entering the temple courts.

groups.note: κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ("his mother's womb") is rendered birth.
The relative ὅν ("whom"), object of the active ἐτίθουν ("they would put"), is rendered he with a passive verb.
The article with the participle ("the one called") is rendered called.
τοῦ αἰτεῖν ἐλεημοσύνην ("to ask for alms") is rendered to beg.
The article with the participle is rendered those entering.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
εἰς ("into") is absorbed into entering.

unmappedTarget.reason: English links the clause to the gate by place; the Greek relative ὅν ("whom") refers to the man.

3:3.sourceText: ὃς ἰδὼν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάνην μέλλοντας εἰσιέναι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἠρώτα ἐλεημοσύνην λαβεῖν.
3:3.targetText: When he saw Peter and John about to enter, he asked them for money.

groups.note: The relative ὅς ("who") is rendered he, as BSB starts a new sentence.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
ἐλεημοσύνην λαβεῖν ("to receive alms") is rendered for money.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat εἰς τὸ ἱερόν ("into the temple") here; the place is clear from 3:2.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for asked; the Greek has none.

3:4.sourceText: ἀτενίσας δὲ Πέτρος εἰς αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ Ἰωάνῃ εἶπεν Βλέψον εἰς ἡμᾶς.
3:4.targetText: Peter looked directly at him, as did John. “Look at us!” said Peter.

groups.note: Πέτρος is the subject of both ἀτενίσας and εἶπεν; BSB names him again with said.
σὺν τῷ Ἰωάνῃ ("with John") is rendered as did John.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:5.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἐπεῖχεν αὐτοῖς προσδοκῶν τι παρ’ αὐτῶν λαβεῖν.
3:5.targetText: So the man gave them his attention, expecting to receive something from them.

groups.note: The article ὁ is used as a pronoun ("he"), rendered the man.
ἐπεῖχεν ("fixed his attention on") is rendered gave … his attention.

3:6.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ Πέτρος Ἀργύριον καὶ χρυσίον οὐχ ὑπάρχει μοι· ὃ δὲ ἔχω, τοῦτό σοι δίδωμι· ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου περιπάτει.
3:6.targetText: But Peter said, “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!”

groups.note: ὑπάρχει μοι ("there is to me") is rendered I do … have.
The dative μοι ("to me") becomes the subject I.
Ναζωραίου ("the Nazarene") is rendered of Nazareth.

unmappedSource.reason: The resumptive τοῦτο ("this") is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra command here; N1904 has only περιπάτει ("walk").

3:7.sourceText: καὶ πιάσας αὐτὸν τῆς δεξιᾶς χειρὸς ἤγειρεν αὐτόν· παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐστερεώθησαν αἱ βάσεις αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ σφυδρά,
3:7.targetText: Taking him by the right hand, Peter helped him up, and at once the man’s feet and ankles were made strong.

groups.note: The genitive χειρός names the part grasped; English adds by.
αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered the man's.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:8.sourceText: καὶ ἐξαλλόμενος ἔστη καὶ περιεπάτει, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν σὺν αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν περιπατῶν καὶ ἁλλόμενος καὶ αἰνῶν τὸν Θεόν.
3:8.targetText: He sprang to his feet and began to walk. Then he went with them into the temple courts, walking and leaping and praising God.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse and is not separately expressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:9.sourceText: καὶ εἶδεν πᾶς ὁ λαὸς αὐτὸν περιπατοῦντα καὶ αἰνοῦντα τὸν Θεόν·
3:9.targetText: When all the people saw him walking and praising God,

groups.note: BSB turns this καί-clause into a When-clause leading into 3:10.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:10.sourceText: ἐπεγίνωσκον δὲ αὐτὸν, ὅτι οὗτος ἦν ὁ πρὸς τὴν ἐλεημοσύνην καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῇ Ὡραίᾳ Πύλῃ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν θάμβους καὶ ἐκστάσεως ἐπὶ τῷ συμβεβηκότι αὐτῷ.
3:10.targetText: they recognized him as the man who used to sit begging at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.

groups.note: ὅτι οὗτος ἦν ("that this was") is rendered as.

targetPhrases.text: the man who used to sit

groups.note: The article with the participle ("the one sitting") is rendered the man who used to sit.
πρὸς τὴν ἐλεημοσύνην ("for alms") is rendered begging.
The article with the participle ("the thing that happened") is rendered what had happened.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed; BSB joins this clause to 3:9 with When.

3:11.sourceText: Κρατοῦντος δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰωάνην συνέδραμεν πᾶς ὁ λαὸς πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ τῇ στοᾷ τῇ καλουμένῃ Σολομῶντος ἔκθαμβοι.
3:11.targetText: While the man clung to Peter and John, all the people were astonished and ran to them in the walkway called Solomon’s Colonnade.

groups.note: The genitive absolute is rendered While … clung to.
αὐτοῦ ("he") is rendered the man.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
στοά ("colonnade, covered walkway") is rendered walkway and named again in Solomon's Colonnade.
The article with the participle ("the one called") is rendered called.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins ran to were astonished, which renders the adjective ἔκθαμβοι ("astonished"); the Greek has no conjunction.

3:12.sourceText: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος ἀπεκρίνατο πρὸς τὸν λαόν Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλεῖται, τί θαυμάζετε ἐπὶ τούτῳ, ἢ ἡμῖν τί ἀτενίζετε ὡς ἰδίᾳ δυνάμει ἢ εὐσεβείᾳ πεποιηκόσιν τοῦ περιπατεῖν αὐτόν;
3:12.targetText: And when Peter saw this, he addressed the people: “Men of Israel, why are you surprised by this? Why do you stare at us as if by our own power or godliness we had made this man walk?

groups.note: Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
ἰδίᾳ ("own") is rendered our own.
The articular infinitive τοῦ περιπατεῖν is rendered walk.
αὐτόν ("him") is rendered this man.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
πρός ("to") is absorbed into addressed.
BSB starts a new question here instead of rendering ἤ ("or").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for saw; the participle ἰδών has none.

3:13.sourceText: ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακώβ, ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, ἐδόξασεν τὸν Παῖδα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ὑμεῖς μὲν παρεδώκατε καὶ ἠρνήσασθε κατὰ πρόσωπον Πειλάτου, κρίναντος ἐκείνου ἀπολύειν·
3:13.targetText: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified His servant Jesus. You handed Him over and rejected Him before Pilate, even though he had decided to release Him.

groups.note: The relative ὅν ("whom") is the object of both verbs; BSB starts a new sentence and repeats it as Him.
κατὰ πρόσωπον ("to the face of") is rendered before.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The genitive absolute is rendered even though he had decided.

3:14.sourceText: ὑμεῖς δὲ τὸν Ἅγιον καὶ Δίκαιον ἠρνήσασθε, καὶ ᾐτήσασθε ἄνδρα φονέα χαρισθῆναι ὑμῖν,
3:14.targetText: You rejected the Holy and Righteous One and asked that a murderer be released to you.

groups.note: ἄνδρα φονέα ("a man, a murderer") is rendered a murderer.

unmappedSource.reason: The μέν … δέ contrast with 3:13 is not separately expressed in this English wording.

3:15.sourceText: τὸν δὲ Ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς ἀπεκτείνατε, ὃν ὁ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, οὗ ἡμεῖς μάρτυρές ἐσμεν.
3:15.targetText: You killed the Author of life, but God raised Him from the dead, and we are witnesses of the fact.

groups.note: The relative ὅν ("whom") is rendered Him, as BSB makes the relative clause a main clause.
The relative οὗ ("of which") is rendered of the fact.

3:16.sourceText: καὶ ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ τοῦτον, ὃν θεωρεῖτε καὶ οἴδατε, ἐστερέωσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἡ πίστις ἡ δι’ αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ τὴν ὁλοκληρίαν ταύτην ἀπέναντι πάντων ὑμῶν.
3:16.targetText: By faith in the name of Jesus, this man whom you see and know has been made strong. It is Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through Him that has given him this complete healing in your presence.

groups.note: The genitive ("faith of the name") is rendered faith in the name.
αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered of Jesus.
The active ἐστερέωσεν ("made strong"), whose subject is τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, is rendered passive; BSB gives the name in the next sentence.
αὐτοῦ ("his") is rendered Jesus'.
The article ἡ before δι’ αὐτοῦ is rendered that.
ἀπέναντι ("before") is rendered in … presence.

3:17.sourceText: καὶ νῦν, ἀδελφοί, οἶδα ὅτι κατὰ ἄγνοιαν ἐπράξατε, ὥσπερ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ὑμῶν·
3:17.targetText: And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did your leaders.

groups.note: ἐπράξατε ("you acted") is understood again with the leaders; BSB repeats it as did.

unmappedSource.reason: The adverbial καί ("also") is not separately expressed in this English wording.

3:18.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς ἃ προκατήγγειλεν διὰ στόματος πάντων τῶν προφητῶν, παθεῖν τὸν Χριστὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπλήρωσεν οὕτως.
3:18.targetText: But in this way God has fulfilled what He foretold through all the prophets, saying that His Christ would suffer.

groups.note: διὰ στόματος ("through the mouth of") is rendered through.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

3:19.sourceText: μετανοήσατε οὖν καὶ ἐπιστρέψατε πρὸς τὸ ἐξαλειφθῆναι ὑμῶν τὰς ἁμαρτίας,
3:19.targetText: Repent, then, and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away,

groups.note: πρὸς τό with the infinitive ("for the purpose of") is rendered so that.

3:20.sourceText: ὅπως ἂν ἔλθωσιν καιροὶ ἀναψύξεως ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ ἀποστείλῃ τὸν προκεχειρισμένον ὑμῖν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν,
3:20.targetText: that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send Jesus, the Christ, who has been appointed for you.

groups.note: ὅπως ἄν ("so that") governs both verbs; BSB repeats that before He may send.
The article with the participle is rendered who has been appointed.

3:21.sourceText: ὃν δεῖ οὐρανὸν μὲν δέξασθαι ἄχρι χρόνων ἀποκαταστάσεως πάντων ὧν ἐλάλησεν ὁ Θεὸς διὰ στόματος τῶν ἁγίων ἀπ’ αἰῶνος αὐτοῦ προφητῶν.
3:21.targetText: Heaven must take Him in until the time comes for the restoration of all things, which God announced long ago through His holy prophets.

groups.note: The relative ὅν ("whom") is rendered Him, as BSB starts a new sentence.
διὰ στόματος ("through the mouth of") is rendered through.
ἀπ’ αἰῶνος ("from of old") is rendered long ago.

3:22.sourceText: Μωϋσῆς μὲν εἶπεν ὅτι Προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀναστήσει Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ὡς ἐμέ· αὐτοῦ ἀκούσεσθε κατὰ πάντα ὅσα ἂν λαλήσῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
3:22.targetText: For Moses said, ‘The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to Him in everything He tells you.

groups.note: πάντα ὅσα ἄν ("all things whatever") is rendered everything.
πρὸς ὑμᾶς ("to you") is rendered you, as the object of tells.

3:23.sourceText: ἔσται δὲ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἥτις ἐὰν μὴ ἀκούσῃ τοῦ προφήτου ἐκείνου ἐξολεθρευθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ.
3:23.targetText: Everyone who does not listen to Him will be completely cut off from among his people.’

groups.note: πᾶσα ψυχή ("every soul") is rendered Everyone.
ἥτις ἐάν ("whoever") is rendered who.
τοῦ προφήτου ἐκείνου ("that prophet") is rendered Him.
The article is used as a possessive.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the introductory ἔσται δέ ("and it will be").

3:24.sourceText: καὶ πάντες δὲ οἱ προφῆται ἀπὸ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν καθεξῆς ὅσοι ἐλάλησαν καὶ κατήγγειλαν τὰς ἡμέρας ταύτας.
3:24.targetText: Indeed, all the prophets from Samuel on, as many as have spoken, have proclaimed these days.

groups.note: καὶ … δέ ("and moreover") is rendered Indeed.
καὶ τῶν καθεξῆς ("and those after him") is rendered on, in from Samuel on.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes have proclaimed the main verb, so this καί ("and") has no separate English word.

3:25.targetText: And you are sons of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your fathers when He said to Abraham, ‘Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.’
